source.title: Routing-Aware Expert Calibration for Machine Unlearning in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
source.authors: Jingyi Xie; Yi-Jun Lin; Yi Xiong; Zhi-Kun Zhang; Sai Li

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates unlearning outcomes on MoE models, including target-task accuracy and retained utility, but does not test whether attacks recover forgotten knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no recovery attacks by fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompting. The routing mismatch analysis and benchmark results are the paper's own; cited recovery or unlearning results are not treated as findings here.
record.test_reason: On MoE models (Qwen1.5-MoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite), the paper reports WMDP accuracy and MMLU utility after several unlearning methods. That bears on the first two clauses of version A in a new architecture setting. It runs no recovery attack, so B–F and A's 'attacks don't recover' clause are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that routing mismatch leaves forget-critical experts under-regularized, and that TRACE improves the forget–utility trade-off on WMDP and MUSE-BOOKS across MoE LLMs. They make no claim about robustness to recovery.
record.recipe_differences: TRACE selects forget-critical experts and reweights retain tokens during MoE unlearning; the paper does not apply a recovery attack recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports higher routing similarity between WMDP-forget and curated WMDP-retain than between WMDP-forget and WikiText. It also reports TRACE robustness to tested γ settings {0.1, 0.5, 1, 10} on MUSE-BOOKS.

fits_no_version.finding: Forget data activates a few MoE experts disproportionately, and those experts get weak retain-data activation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MoE unlearning, a forget–retain routing mismatch leaves forget-critical experts under-regularized.

fits_no_version.finding: Domain-matched WMDP-retain data has higher routing similarity to WMDP-forget than WikiText does.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The choice of retain set changes routing overlap with the forget set in MoE models.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen3-30B-A3B, MUSE-BOOKS VerbMem and KnowMem on the forget set drop after unlearning, and TRACE keeps retain KnowMem (65.97).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoE unlearning methods reduce MUSE memorization metrics while varying in retain utility; no recovery attack is tested.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are evaluated, so the paper cannot establish whether unlearned knowledge is recoverable or removed. The paper states that small forget sets may make routing estimates noisy. The routing-frequency and routing-similarity results are shown in figures without values transcribed in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional WMDP Bio and Cyber accuracy rows separately in Table 1, ablation variants and repeated benchmark results in Tables 3–5, and γ sensitivity results in Figure 5. These were left out to stay within the 60-row limit after retaining aggregate WMDP results, all MUSE-BOOKS main-table metrics, and routing findings; the omitted results do not report recovery attacks.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks (relearning, ablation, quantization, prompting) recover WMDP knowledge after any method, including TRACE.
All: no activation-direction ablation or blocked-versus-deleted analysis.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context probe.
TRACE is a new method, but the paper makes no robustness-to-attack claim and runs no attack.

missing.what: GradDiff with domain-specific WMDP-retain data (GradDiff*) compared with TRACE on forget quality and MMLU; figure only, not declared in rows_left_out

record.verdict_notes: Classed as a test of A only in a narrow sense: new MoE setting, forgetting and utility clauses only. The attack clause, the core of the shallow-unlearning question, is untested, so these results cannot show unlearning is deep. Most A rows compare the study's own method with baselines, so treat the supports label as a benchmark-level result.

versions.untested_parts: The WMDP target-accuracy and MMLU utility components are tested. Whether simple attacks recover the target knowledge is not tested.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning recovery attack is reported.
No activation-direction ablation or test of blocked access versus deleted knowledge is reported.
No weight quantization recovery test is reported.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery test is reported.
TRACE is proposed to improve forgetting and utility, but the paper does not test resistance to the attacks named in the claim.

source_check.notes: All 24 values match Table 1 (Acc-Avg is the mean of Cyber and Bio; WikiText retain set; chat checkpoints). No recovery attack of any kind is run, so only A's forgetting and utility clauses are tested. SEUF and ESFT lose 6-11 MMLU points, so l0 should be split, with TRACE alone supporting.

statements.correction: TRACE WMDP Acc-Avg 0.2706 (Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat) and 0.2636 (DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat) vs Origin 0.5390/0.4903; MMLU 0.5819/0.5541 vs 0.5954/0.5672. TRACE rows: W13, W14, W27, W28. Qwen GA/GradDiff/NPO MMLU 0.3217/0.2295/0.2481 are right; DeepSeek GradDiff Acc-Avg 0.3131.
statements.problem: TRACE's WMDP Acc-Avg is given as 0.25-0.28, but that is the TRACE/ESFT/SEUF range (0.2494-0.2827); TRACE alone is 0.2706/0.2636. Cited rows W9-W12 and W23 are SEUF/ESFT rows; TRACE rows W13, W14, W27 are not cited. DeepSeek GradDiff does not reach chance (0.3131).

statements.correction: 2606.10338 runs no attack of any kind. MMLU vs Origin 0.5954/0.5672 (Qwen1.5-MoE/DeepSeek-V2-Lite): TRACE 0.5819/0.5541, ESFT 0.5319/0.5099, SEUF 0.4915/0.4553. The authors say SEUF's setting can degrade model utility.
statements.problem: It is right that no attack is run on TRACE, ESFT or SEUF. But this study does not show 'MMLU kept' for SEUF (down 10-11 points) or fully for ESFT (down about 6).
